+/-! # Comparing resolution classes with the homology of derived global sections
+
+Source: Stacks Project, Tags 01DZ and 0FKU.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+universe u
+set_option autoImplicit false
+set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
+set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types false
+set_option synthInstance.maxSize 2048
+open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory Opposite
+open AlgebraicGeometry TopologicalSpace
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules
+noncomputable section
+
+variable (X : Scheme.{u})
+  [HasDerivedCategory.{u} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
+
+local instance : CommRing ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤)) :=
+  inferInstanceAs (CommRing Γ(X, ⊤))
+
+/-- Derived global sections of a coefficient sheaf placed in degree zero. -/
+abbrev cupDerivedSections (F : X.Modules) :=
+  (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).rightDerivedFunctor.obj
+    ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
+      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj F)
+
+/-- A comparison with derived global sections, including the representative formula.
+The cycles in integer degrees are obtained by the actual extension by zero. -/
+structure CupDerivedClassComparison where
+  equiv : ∀ (F : X.Modules) (n : ℕ),
+    (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace n).obj F ≃ₗ[Γ(X, ⊤)]
+      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, ⊤)) (n : ℤ)).obj
+        (cupDerivedSections X F)
+  on_cycles : ∀ {F : X.Modules} (D : CupAcyclicResolution F) (n : ℕ)
+    (a : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
+      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
+    let K := ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
+      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj D.integerComplex
+    ∃ z : K.cycles (n : ℤ),
+      ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).map
+        (D.K.extendXIso ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat (by rfl)).hom) (K.iCycles n z) =
+          a.val ∧
+      equiv F n (D.class n a) =
+        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, ⊤)) (n : ℤ)).map
+          (moduleCup_globalComparison X D.integerComplex ≫
+            (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).rightDerivedFunctor.map
+              (inv D.derivedAugmentation))
+          (cupLocalizedCycleClass K n z)
+
+/-- The right-derived cohomology functor agrees with homology of RΓ, with its
+canonical formula on every computing resolution.
+Source: Stacks Project, Tag 01DZ, computation by injective resolutions;
+Tag 0FKU, global specialization of the comparison diagram.
+(blueprint: lem-sc-module-cup-derived-class-comparison)
+Proof: choose an injective resolution of F and extend it by zero to integers.
+This bounded-below complex of injectives is K-injective, so the right-derived
+comparison unit at it is invertible. The localized augmentation is invertible
+as well. The homology factorization of localization and the extension homology
+isomorphism therefore identify H^n(RΓ(F[0])) with H^n(Γ(I)). Compose with the
+inverse of I.isoRightDerivedObj to obtain equiv, in the displayed direction.
+For another computing resolution D, extend D.comparison by zero. Its equation
+over the augmentation and naturality of the derived comparison identify the
+localized composite with the chosen comparison above. The map on global
+homology is precisely the one in D.class; computes says it is invertible.
+The extension cycles isomorphism lifts a to z and identifies its component
+through extendXIso. Naturality of homologyπ then gives the displayed equation.
+Independence of the injective resolution follows from comparison maps over F
+and their homotopies. At n=0 extension has a zero incoming differential, just
+as the natural complex does; zero sheaves and zero cycles cause no exception. -/
+theorem exists_cupDerivedClassComparison : Nonempty (CupDerivedClassComparison X) := by sorry
+
+end
+end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules

+/-! # Tensoring homology classes in the derived category of modules
+
+Source: Stacks Project, Tags 0FKU and 068G.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+universe u
+set_option autoImplicit false
+open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory
+open scoped TensorProduct
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules
+noncomputable section
+
+variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k] [HasDerivedCategory.{u} (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
+
+/-- The class of an integer-degree cycle, transported through the homology
+factorization of localization. This uses only actual homology and an existing iso. -/
+def cupLocalizedCycleClass (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} k) ℤ) (n : ℤ)
+    (z : K.cycles n) :
+    (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) n).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) :=
+  ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors (ModuleCat.{u} k) n).app K).inv
+    (K.homologyπ n z)
+
+/-- The natural tensor of derived homology classes, normalized on cochain cycles.
+This is an interface, rather than a choice of an unproved operation. -/
+structure CupDerivedHomologyTensor (k : Type u) [CommRing k]
+    [HasDerivedCategory.{u} (ModuleCat.{u} k)] where
+  pair : ∀ (A B : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (p q : ℕ),
+    (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) (p : ℤ)).obj A →ₗ[k]
+      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) (q : ℤ)).obj B →ₗ[k]
+        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) ((p + q : ℕ) : ℤ)).obj (A ⊗ B)
+  natural : ∀ (A A' B B' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} k))
+    (f : A ⟶ A') (g : B ⟶ B') (p q : ℕ)
+    (a : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) (p : ℤ)).obj A)
+    (b : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) (q : ℤ)).obj B),
+    pair A' B' p q
+        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) (p : ℤ)).map f a)
+        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) (q : ℤ)).map g b) =
+      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) ((p + q : ℕ) : ℤ)).map (f ⊗ₘ g)
+        (pair A B p q a b)
+  on_cycles : ∀ (K L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} k) ℤ) (p q : ℕ)
+    (a : K.cycles p) (b : L.cycles q),
+    ∃ z : (K ⊗ L).cycles (p + q),
+      (K ⊗ L).iCycles (p + q) z =
+        (HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj K L p q (p + q) (by omega))
+          ((K.iCycles p a) ⊗ₜ[k] (L.iCycles q b)) ∧
+      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) ((p + q : ℕ) : ℤ)).map
+          (Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ DerivedCategory.Q K L)
+          (pair (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L) p q
+            (cupLocalizedCycleClass K p a) (cupLocalizedCycleClass L q b)) =
+        cupLocalizedCycleClass (K ⊗ L) (p + q) z
+
+/-- Derived homology admits its natural bilinear tensor pairing.
+Source: Stacks Project, Tag 0FKU, global cohomology diagram following Lemma 20.31.3;
+Tag 068G, tensor product of cocycles.
+(blueprint: lem-sc-module-cup-derived-homology-tensor)
+Proof: represent a class in H^p(A) by a morphism k[-p] to A. The rank-one free
+module k is projective, so the standard homology/Hom identification is bijective.
+Tensor the two representing morphisms and use the canonical identification
+k[-p-q] with k[-p] tensor k[-q]. Transport back to homology. Additivity and
+k-linearity of tensor give a bilinear map; composition gives naturality.
+For localized complexes, the two representing maps are the single-complex maps
+whose components are the supplied cocycles. Their tensor, followed by the lax
+localization comparison, has component the indicated tensor summand. The signed
+Leibniz rule says that component is a cycle. Applying homology gives on_cycles.
+The same argument includes degree zero, zero complexes and zero
+cycles; projectivity is used for the rank-one source, never for K or L. -/
+theorem exists_cupDerivedHomologyTensor : Nonempty (CupDerivedHomologyTensor k) := by sorry
+
+end
+end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules

+/-! # Homology represented by a single free module
+
+Source: Stacks Project, Tag 064B (K-projective complexes), and Tag 068G.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+universe u
+set_option autoImplicit false
+open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules
+noncomputable section
+
+/-- The free rank-one module in degree n, also denoted k[-n]. -/
+abbrev cupSingleModule (k : Type u) [CommRing k] (n : ℤ) :=
+  (HomologicalComplex.single (ModuleCat.{u} k) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n).obj
+    (ModuleCat.of k k)
+
+variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] [HasDerivedCategory.{u} (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
+
+/-- Homology represented by the shifted free module, with the cocycle normalization.
+No representative or derived object is selected by this interface. -/
+structure CupHomologyRepresentability where
+  equiv : ∀ (A : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℤ),
+    (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cupSingleModule k n) ⟶ A) ≃ₗ[k]
+      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) n).obj A
+  natural : ∀ (A B : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℤ)
+    (f : DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cupSingleModule k n) ⟶ A) (g : A ⟶ B),
+    equiv B n (f ≫ g) = (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) n).map g
+      (equiv A n f)
+  on_cycles : ∀ (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} k) ℤ) (n : ℤ)
+    (f : cupSingleModule k n ⟶ K) (z : K.cycles n),
+    ((HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n (ModuleCat.of k k)).inv ≫
+      f.f n) (1 : k) = K.iCycles n z →
+    equiv (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) n (DerivedCategory.Q.map f) =
+      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors (ModuleCat.{u} k) n).app K).inv
+        (K.homologyπ n z)
+
+/-- Hom from k[-n] naturally identifies with H^n, including its value on cocycles.
+Source: Stacks Project, Tag 064B, the K-projective localization description;
+Tag 068G, representing a cohomology class by a cocycle.
+(blueprint: lem-sc-module-cup-homology-representability)
+Proof: the single complex k[-n] is bounded above and consists of projectives,
+so it is K-projective. Morphisms from its localization to Q(K) are chain maps
+modulo chain homotopy. A chain map is determined by the image of 1 in degree n,
+which is a cycle, and a homotopy changes this image by a boundary. Thus evaluation
+at 1 identifies the quotient with H^n(K), bijectively and k-linearly. Every derived
+object has a representative, and the identification commutes with quasi-isomorphisms,
+so it descends to every A. Postcomposition gives naturality. For a chain map f
+with the displayed cycle z, evaluation is homology projection of z; transport by
+homologyFunctorFactors gives exactly on_cycles. This works in every integer degree,
+for unbounded K, the zero ring and zero cycles; no projectivity of K is required. -/
+theorem exists_cupHomologyRepresentability : Nonempty (CupHomologyRepresentability k) := by sorry
+
+end
+end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules

+/-! # The normalized tensor of shifted free rank-one modules
+
+Source: Stacks Project, Tag 068G, the tensor-of-cocycles construction.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+universe u
+set_option autoImplicit false
+open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory
+open scoped TensorProduct
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules
+noncomputable section
+
+variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] [HasDerivedCategory.{u} (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
+
+/-- The shifted-unit tensor identification with its representative formula.
+Source: Stacks Project, Tag 068G, equation-simple-tor-product and its construction;
+Tag 0FKU, the localization comparison for tensor products.
+(blueprint: lem-sc-module-cup-shifted-unit-tensor)
+Proof: the tensor of the two single free complexes is zero outside degree p+q.
+In that degree use k tensor k = k, with inverse taking 1 to 1 tensor 1, to construct
+an isomorphism from the single free complex in degree p+q. Both single complexes
+are K-flat, so the lax localization comparison on them is invertible. Compose Q
+of the complex isomorphism with its inverse to obtain e. For maps f and g into
+arbitrary complexes K and L, let h be the complex isomorphism followed by f tensor g.
+The degree p+q component of h sends 1 to the displayed tensor summand. Naturality
+of the lax tensor comparison gives the displayed derived-morphism equation, since
+the comparison on the single complexes cancels with its inverse. Hence if f and g
+represent cycles, h represents their tensor cycle, without any additional sign.
+This argument includes p=0, q=0, negative degrees, the zero ring and zero maps;
+no flatness of K or L is needed. -/
+theorem exists_cupShiftedUnitTensor (p q : ℤ) :
+    ∃ e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cupSingleModule k (p + q)) ≅
+      DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cupSingleModule k p) ⊗
+        DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cupSingleModule k q),
+    ∀ (K L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} k) ℤ)
+      (f : cupSingleModule k p ⟶ K) (g : cupSingleModule k q ⟶ L),
+    ∃ h : cupSingleModule k (p + q) ⟶ K ⊗ L,
+      ((HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (p + q)
+          (ModuleCat.of k k)).inv ≫ h.f (p + q)) (1 : k) =
+        (HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj K L p q (p + q) rfl)
+          ((((HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℤ) p
+              (ModuleCat.of k k)).inv ≫ f.f p) (1 : k)) ⊗ₜ[k]
+            (((HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℤ) q
+              (ModuleCat.of k k)).inv ≫ g.f q) (1 : k))) ∧
+      e.hom ≫ (DerivedCategory.Q.map f ⊗ₘ DerivedCategory.Q.map g) ≫
+          Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ DerivedCategory.Q K L = DerivedCategory.Q.map h := by sorry
+
+end
+end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules

+/-! # Evaluating one realized pairing in derived homology
+
+Source: Stacks Project, Section 20.31, Tags 0FKU and 0FKV.
+(blueprint: lem-sc-module-cup-single-pairing-homology)
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section

+

+  cupRealizationHasColimitsOfSize cupRealizationMonoidalPreadditive cupRealizationMonoidalClosed
+  cupRealizationHasFunctorialFlatResolution cupRealizationIsGrothendieckAbelian

+  inferInstanceAs (CommRing Γ(X, ⊤))
+
+attribute [local irreducible] Functor.rightDerivedFunctor moduleCup_globalComparison
+
+/-- A single realized pairing is evaluated by the tensor operation on derived
+homology and the supplied global cup diagram.
+Source: Stacks Project, Tag 0FKU, Lemma 20.31.3 and its global specialization.
+(blueprint: lem-sc-module-cup-single-pairing-homology)
+Proof: use J.on_cycles to extend the two input cycles and the output cycle to
+integer degrees. Apply hdiagram to the two integer resolution complexes.
+Postcompose it with RΓ(Q(t)) and RΓ(inv target.derivedAugmentation).
+Naturality of the comparison moves Q(t) past the target comparison; hnatural
+moves the two input augmentations across μ. Thus the bottom composite is
+μ on the coefficient objects, followed by RΓ(D.derivedMap t).
+Use V.natural for the input comparisons, and V.on_cycles for their localized
+integer cycles. The section formula for ν and ht identify the image of the
+tensor cycle with the extended output cycle: after extendXIso its component is
+D.pair p q top a.val b.val, which equals c.val by hc. Injectivity of the cycle
+inclusion gives equality of those cycles. Naturality of homologyπ and of the
+homology factorization then identify the upper composite with J.equiv applied
+to D.target.class. The input formulas from J.on_cycles identify the other
+composite with the right side below. No comparison of two resolutions, equality
+of input classes, or normalization of the derived morphism is assumed. The
+argument also applies when p or q is zero, since extension by zero and the tensor
+summand formula hold in those degrees without a predecessor. -/
+theorem moduleCup_single_pairing_homology
+    (V : CupDerivedHomologyTensor Γ(X, ⊤)) (J : CupDerivedClassComparison X)
+    (μ : ∀ A B : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)),
+    (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).rightDerivedFunctor.obj A ⊗
+      (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).rightDerivedFunctor.obj B ⟶
+        (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).rightDerivedFunctor.obj (A ⊗ B))
+    (hnatural : ∀ (A A' B B' : DerivedCategory
+    (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))) (f : A ⟶ A') (g : B ⟶ B'),
+    ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).rightDerivedFunctor.map f ⊗ₘ
+      (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).rightDerivedFunctor.map g) ≫
+        μ A' B' = μ A B ≫
+          (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).rightDerivedFunctor.map (f ⊗ₘ g))
+    (hdiagram : ∀ K L : CochainComplex
+    (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ,
+    let T := (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
+      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
+    let R := (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).rightDerivedFunctor
+    ∃ ν : T.obj K ⊗ T.obj L ⟶ T.obj (K ⊗ L),
+      (∀ (i j n : ℤ) (h : i + j = n) (x : Γ(K.X i, ⊤)) (y : Γ(L.X j, ⊤)),
+        (ν.f n).hom
+            ((HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj (T.obj K) (T.obj L) i j n h).hom
+              (TensorProduct.tmul Γ(X, ⊤) x y)) =
+          (HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj K L i j n h).val.app (op ⊤)
+            (tmulSection x y)) ∧
+      (moduleCup_globalComparison X K ⊗ₘ moduleCup_globalComparison X L) ≫
+          μ (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L) ≫
+          R.map (Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ DerivedCategory.Q K L) =
+        Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ DerivedCategory.Q (T.obj K) (T.obj L) ≫
+          DerivedCategory.Q.map ν ≫ moduleCup_globalComparison X (K ⊗ L))
+    {F G : X.Modules}
+    (D : CupResolutionPairing F G)
+    (t : D.left.integerComplex ⊗ D.right.integerComplex ⟶ D.target.integerComplex)
+    (ht : D.Realizes t) (p q : ℕ)
+    (a : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
+      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.left.K).sc p).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
+    (b : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
+      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.right.K).sc q).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
+    (c : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
+      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.target.K).sc (p + q)).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
+    (hc : c.val = D.pair p q ⊤ a.val b.val) :
+    J.equiv (F ⊗ G) (p + q) (D.target.class (p + q) c) =
+      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, ⊤)) ((p + q : ℕ) : ℤ)).map
+        (μ ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
+            (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj F)
+          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
+            (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj G) ≫
+          (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).rightDerivedFunctor.map
+            (D.derivedMap t))
+        (V.pair (cupDerivedSections X F) (cupDerivedSections X G) p q
+          (J.equiv F p (D.left.class p a)) (J.equiv G q (D.right.class q b))) := by sorry
+
+end
